intelligence.human_view: Think of a house where every door handle is the same handle: you never have to learn it twice, your hand knows it in the dark. That is what one bar and one icon set do — the same six tiles, the same colors, the same white glyphs in the middle, on every page, so a citizen moving between rooms never meets a different icon for the same thing. And think of the difference between the real post office and a painted front: a MAIL tap must open the mail they actually live in, not a copy standing in front of it. The same honesty runs through the rest: a demographics form with no switch is a door with no handle — you can fill it in and still be invisible — and a people row whose percentage wanders with the name is a row that breaks the moment a long name arrives. A phone screen that cannot hold its own navigation is not a page yet, however good it looks on a laptop. And underneath all of it, the simplest law of all: carry his words exactly. "Delay" means delay. A retelling that upgrades a word into a shutdown stops the whole machine on a word he never said. The work is not paused, the review is now, the doing is now — complete and done is the only finished state he accepts.
intelligence.simple_view: One bar sits at the bottom of every page. It has the same six tiles in the same colors, with white pictures in the middle. A tap on MAIL takes you to your real mail, not a copy. The people rows show a name, a number at the top right, and five big buttons below. A phone screen must fit everything on it, or the page is not done. His words stay exactly as he said them. When something needs doing, we do it now.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the little bar at the bottom is the same on every page now — the same six colored tiles, the same white pictures in the middle, the same little black ball with the white number tucked neatly inside its tile. When you tap MAIL, it takes you to your real mail, the one you actually use, never to a pretend copy of it. The questions about who you are — your age, where you are from, your language — will each have their own little switch, so you can choose to be found or stay private, and your location is never shared. Each person in your list gets two tidy lines: their name up top with the number locked in the corner, and five bigger buttons below, the little eye first so you can see who they are before you write to them. And the phone screen must hold everything neatly — if the buttons run off the edge, the page is not finished. His words are carried exactly as he spoke them, nothing added, nothing widened. What needs reviewing is reviewed now, what needs doing is done now, and done means complete and done.
intelligence.naya_view: Make set three the official bottom bar on every page — same set, same colors, same white glyphs, same ball inset in the tile — and let no page keep another set after its round lands. Render all six bottom-bar glyphs white in the center of their tiles, from one source, on Dashboard, Personal, Calendar, walkthrough, Business, and Space; the tile keeps its deep color and rim light, the glyph is never the tile's color. Route every MAIL tap to the actual Smart Mail at nayanet.app/rooms/mail, never to an in-place mail mode; build no mail-sending from inside pages until he picks the privacy-rule change or the Edge Function. Build the per-demographic on/off switches in Personal Settings — age, where you are from, ethnicity, language, interests — working, persisting, and respected, with location never shared; a question without a switch is a form with no function. Build every people row as two lines — orb top-left, name beside it, percentage locked top-right always; five buttons a little bigger on line two, eye first, then Messenger, Mail, Audio, Video — with a hard max on username length so a longer name shortens gracefully and the board is never redone for a long name. Walk every calendar view whole at 390 before it is called done; carry his calendar rulings as rulings and send no link to Shawn until the eye passes. Carry his words verbatim in every retelling — never widen a word into a bigger action than the one he said, and when a word could mean two things, the smaller reading holds until he confirms the bigger one. Review now, do now, and call a thing done only when it is complete and proven.
